## Landed (5)

| id | signature | summary |
|---|---|---|
| `date_add_months` | `DateAddMonths::run() -> u16` | Steps a Gregorian (year, month, day) forward or backward by a whole number of months (direction 0=forward/add, 1=backward/subtract, magnitude months: u16), clamping the result day to the target month's real length in one direct jump (e.g. Jan 31 stepped forward 1 month lands on Feb 28/29, never Mar 3, and Jan 31 stepped forward 2 months lands squarely on Mar 31 with no intermediate Feb clamp) -- the shared foundation the whole Excel COUP* family (COUPNCD, COUPPCD, COUPDAYBS, COUPDAYS, COUPDAYSNC, COUPNUM) walks backward over in (12/frequency)-month increments, distinct from days_between (spans whole days, not months) and is_valid_date (checks a given date, doesn't derive a new one). |
| `day_count_30_360_eu` | `DayCount30360Eu::run() -> u16` | European (ISDA) 30/360 day count from (y1,m1,d1) to (y2,m2,d2): day-of-month 31 on EITHER date is clamped to 30 independently of the other date (Excel's DAYS360 with method=TRUE) -- unlike day_count_30_360_us, D2's clamp never depends on whether D1 was 30 or 31, so there is no conditional chain at all, just days = (Y2-Y1)*360 + (M2-M1)*30 + (D2-D1), returned as a (magnitude, sign) pair since an end date before the start date is a valid negative span, not an error. |
| `day_count_act_360` | `DayCountAct360::run() -> u16` | Actual/360 day-count year fraction: actual calendar days between two Gregorian dates (days_between's own Rata-Die serial-day technique, reused here) divided by a fixed 360-day year -- the plainest of the five day-count conventions, with no month-length adjustment unlike 30/360 US/European and no actual/365 or actual/actual denominator swap. |
| `day_count_act_365` | `DayCountAct365::run() -> u16` | Actual/365 Fixed day-count year fraction between two Gregorian dates: actual calendar days elapsed (days_between's Rata-Die serial-day technique, reused here) divided by a FIXED 365-day year every time -- never 366, even across a leap year, which is what makes this Actual/365 Fixed and distinct from Actual/Actual (prorates against each date's own real 365- or 366-day year) and from Actual/360 (fixed 360-day divisor instead); equivalent to Excel's YEARFRAC(start_date, end_date, 3). |
| `day_count_act_act` | `DayCountActAct::run() -> u16` | Actual/Actual day-count year fraction between two dates: the numerator is the real calendar day count (days_between's own Rata-Die serial-day technique, inlined -- each cell compiles standalone against the shared kernel prelude only, so cross-cell logic is duplicated rather than called), the denominator is 366 if the actual-day span includes a Feb 29 and 365 otherwise -- a single well-defined simplification of the multi-period ISDA actual/actual standard (whose coupon-frequency-weighted subtleties are out of scope for a tiny cell), returned as an unreduced num/den pair so the caller can see which basis applied -- distinct from this pack's forthcoming fixed-denominator actual/360 and actual/365 siblings by deriving its denominator from the span's own leap-day content instead of a constant. |
